| Answer | Marks |

| Interpreting $\rho ( t ) c ^ { 2 }$ as total energy density, and substituting $\frac { p ( t ) } { c ^ { 2 } } = w \rho ( t )$ into the $2^{\text{nd}}$ Friedmann equation yields: $\dot { \rho } + 3 \rho ( 1 + w ) \frac { \dot { a } } { a } = 0$ | 0.1 |
| $\rho \propto a ^ { - 3 ( w + 1 ) }$ | 0.2 |

| (iii) For a constant energy density, let say $\epsilon = \text{constant}$, $\epsilon _ { \Lambda } \propto a ^ { 0 }$ so that $w _ { \Lambda } = - 1$ | 0.3 |

Question A.4

| Answer | Marks |
| --- | --- |
| (i) In case of $k = 0$, for radiation we have $\rho_r a^4 = \text{constant}$. So by comparing the parameters values with their present value, $\rho_r(t) a^4(t) = \rho_{r0} a_0^4$,

$$\left( \frac{\dot{a}}{a} \right)^2 = \frac{8\pi G}{3} \rho_{r0} \left( \frac{a_0}{a} \right)^4$$

$$\int a\, da = \frac{1}{2} a^2 + K = \left( \frac{8\pi G}{3} \rho_{r0} a_0^4 \right)^{\frac{1}{2}} t$$ | 0.2 |
| Because $a(t=0) = 0$, $K = 0$, then

$$a(t) = (2)^{\frac{1}{2}} \left( \frac{8\pi G}{3} \rho_{r0} a_0^4 \right)^{\frac{1}{4}} t^{\frac{1}{2}} = (2H_0)^{\frac{1}{2}} t^{\frac{1}{2}}$$

where $H_0 = \left( \frac{8\pi G}{3} \rho_{r0} \right)^{\frac{1}{2}}$ after taking $a_0 = 1$ | 0.2 |
| (ii) for non-relativistic matter domination, using $\rho_m(t) a^3(t) = \rho_{m0} a_0^3$, and similar way we will get

$$a(t) = \left( \frac{3}{2} \right)^{\frac{2}{3}} \left( \frac{8\pi G}{3} \rho_{m0} a_0^4 \right)^{\frac{1}{3}} t^{\frac{2}{3}} = \left( \frac{3H_0}{2} \right)^{\frac{2}{3}} t^{\frac{2}{3}}$$

where $H_0 = \left( \frac{8\pi G}{3} \rho_{m0} \right)^{\frac{1}{2}}$ | 0.4 |
| (iii) for constant energy density, $\ln a = H_0 t + K'$

where $H_0 = \left( \frac{8\pi G}{3} \rho_\Lambda \right)^{\frac{1}{2}}$ and $K'$ is integration constant. Taking condition $a_0 = 1$, $\ln\left( \frac{a}{a_0} \right) = H_0 (t - t_0)$

$$a(t) = e^{H_0 (t - t_0)}$$ | 0.4 |
| Total | 1.2 |
| Answer Condition for critical energy condition: | Marks |
| $\rho_c(t) = \frac{3H^2}{8\pi G}$ Friedmann equation can be written as

$$H^2(t) = H^2(t) \Omega(t) - \frac{kc^2}{R^2 a^2(t)}$$ | 0.1 |

questions.answer:
（i）辐射主导：$a(t) = (2H_0)^{\frac{1}{2}} t^{\frac{1}{2}}$

（ii）物质主导：$a(t) = \left( \frac{3H_0}{2} \right)^{\frac{2}{3}} t^{\frac{2}{3}}$

（iii）常数能量密度：$a(t) = e^{H_0 (t - t_0)}$

临界条件：$\rho_c(t) = \frac{3H^2}{8\pi G}$，$\frac{R^2 a^2 H^2 (\Omega - 1)}{c^2} = k$

Inflation period can be generated by constant energy period, therefore it is a $p = w \rho c^2 = -\rho c^2$ phase where $w = -1$ so that (negative pressure). Differentiating Friedmann equation leads to0.2 0.4
$\dot{a}^2 = \frac{8\pi G}{3}\rho a^2 - \frac{kc^2}{R_0^2}$，$\frac{8\pi G}{3}p\left(-3\rho a^2 + 2\rho a\dot{a}\right)$：$2\dot{a}\ddot{a} = \frac{8\pi G}{3}\left(a\dot{a} + 2\rho a\right)$，$\ddot{a} = -\frac{4\pi G}{3}\left(\rho + \frac{3p}{c^2}\right)$

questions.answer: > 暴胀由恒定能量密度阶段产生，对应状态方程 $p = w\rho c^2 = -\rho c^2$（$w=-1$，负压）。由 Friedmann 方程求导可得 $\ddot{a} = -\frac{4\pi G}{3}\left(\rho + \frac{3p}{c^2}\right)$，代入 $p = -\rho c^2$ 得 $\ddot{a} > 0$，即加速膨胀，等价于 $\frac{d(Ha)^{-1}}{dt} < 0$（哈勃半径收缩）。

questions.content:
Question D.2

From equations (C.1.1), (C.1.2) and (C.1.3) we can obtain

$$N = - \left[ \frac{\phi}{M_{pl}} \right]^2 \frac{1}{2n} + \beta$$

where $\beta$ is a integration constant. As $N = 0$ at $\phi_{end}$ then $\beta = \frac{n}{4}$.

$$N = - \left[ \frac{\phi}{M_{pl}} \right]^2 \frac{1}{2n} + \frac{n}{4}$$

$$\eta_{V}=n(n-1)\left[\frac{M_{pl}}{\phi}\right]^{2}=\frac{2(n-1)}{n-4N}$$

$$\varepsilon = \frac{n^{2}}{2}\left[\frac{M_{pl}}{\phi}\right]^{2} = \frac{n}{n - 4N}$$

so that

$$r = 16\varepsilon = \frac{16n}{n - 4N}$$

$$n_{s} = 1 + 2 \eta_{V} - 6 \epsilon = 1 - \frac{2(n+2)}{(n - 4N)}$$

To obtain the observational constraint we need $n_{s} = 0.968$, $r < 0.12$. There is no a closest integer n that is inconsistent with the condition $r < 0.12$. As example, for $n = -6$ leads a contradiction $0 < (-0.2)(-0.27)$ and for $n = -5$ leads a contradiction.
